clue.text: Purists needing education to wear trousers

indicators.note: to wear something is to have it around you, so the trousers go round the education

parts.note: pants is the American (and informal) word for trousers

explanation.surface: Fussy traditionalists who need some schooling before they can put their trousers on.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedants insist on strict correctness, which makes them purists about rules and detail.

clue.text: Scientist from site oddly imprisoned by a German twice

indicators.note: imprisoned by means held inside, so the picked letters go between the two German words
twice says the German word appears two times

parts.note: ein is the German for a

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first and third

explanation.surface: A scientist is spirited out of a building and held captive by a German, twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, the physicist of relativity, is the archetypal scientist.

clue.text: Innocent answer that provides flavour

parts.note: angelic means pure and innocent

explanation.surface: A naive reply that adds some spice to a conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica is an aromatic herb whose candied stems and roots are used to flavour cakes and liqueurs.

clue.text: Short-lived politician suppressed by terrible strain

indicators.note: suppressed by means held down under, so in this down entry the politician comes below
terrible means awful, so the letters of strain are put into disorder

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A politician whose career was cut short, crushed by unbearable pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transitory passes quickly and does not last, so it is short-lived.

clue.text: Cheers team transport

parts.note: ta and cheers are both informal British ways to say thank you
XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a team in cricket or football

explanation.surface: Thanking a sports team for laying on their travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car carrying passengers, a means of transport.

clue.text: Cut energy, being harsh

parts.note: to sever is to cut through
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Cutting the power supply is a harsh measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe treatment is strict, stern and unsparing, so harsh.

clue.text: Top cover from hospital broadcast on web

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
to air a programme is to broadcast it
a net is a mesh or web

explanation.surface: A best-selling blanket from a hospital, advertised online.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine mesh worn over the hair keeps it in place, so it covers the top of the head.

clue.text: Poles overwhelmed by divine being's stupidness

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swamped or engulfed, so the poles go inside

parts.note: a deity is a divine being; the 's is read as 'has' or ignored
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: People from Poland are crushed by a god's foolishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like a nationality, but it means the two magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Density in the sense of thickness of mind is a colloquial word for slowness or stupidity.

clue.text: Steep service charge applied to staff

indicators.note: applied to means put next to, so the charge follows the staff

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff of office
a rate is a charge levied for local services, as in British council rates

explanation.surface: A complaint that a restaurant's service charge on top of staff wages is too steep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective about the price, but it is the verb meaning to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak it in liquid until it softens, which is exactly what macerating does.

clue.text: A German trained as manager, for example

definitions.text: A German trained as manager, for example

parts.words: A German trained as manager, for example
parts.note: the letters of 'a German' rearranged spell 'manager', and that kind of letter shuffle is the thing the clue names

explanation.surface: A German national who has been through training to become a manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trained' hints at shuffled letters: rearrange A GERMAN and you get MANAGER. The clue describes that wordplay device itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning one word or phrase into another by rearranging its letters is the very device described.

clue.text: Degree of penalty skills?

parts.note: a fine is a monetary penalty
arts are skills, as in the arts of persuasion

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether a footballer's penalty-taking ability merits a qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A university course in painting, sculpture and the like leads to a degree of that name.

clue.text: Amusing aspects will include debt

indicators.note: include means take in, so the debt goes inside the aspects

parts.note: facets are aspects or sides of something
an IOU, I owe you, is a written acknowledgement of debt

explanation.surface: Funny parts of a story will mention money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Facetious remarks treat serious matters with flippant humour, meant to be amusing.

clue.text: Shots subdue son

parts.note: to still something is to calm or subdue it
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A parent fires shots, or gives an injection, to subdue their son.
explanation.definitionFit: Stills are photographs, especially single frames from a film, and a photograph is a shot.

clue.text: Innovative thinker once dismissing king not making sense

indicators.note: innovative means newly made or reworked, so these letters are put into a new order
dismissing means sending away, so a letter is taken out of the word thinker

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A former visionary has sacked a monarch, and the result is muddled nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innovative thinker' reads as a phrase for an inventor, but 'Innovative' is the anagram signal. 'dismissing' removes K from THINKER, leaving THINER, and that plus ONCE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech or writing that is unclear and fails to hold together logically does not make sense.

clue.text: Tough foes do badly with no time for church

indicators.note: badly means poorly done, so the letters are scrambled
with no means without, so a letter is removed from the word tough

explanation.surface: Hardened enemies fare poorly, having no time for religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes T from TOUGH, leaving OUGH; with FOES DO that is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A church is a building dedicated to worship, traditionally called the house of God.

clue.text: Find missing past record

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so one word is taken away from the other

parts.note: to discover is to find
over means past, finished, as in the game is over

explanation.surface: An instruction to track down an old recording that has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes OVER out of DISCOVER, leaving DISC.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat disc, and a disc is also a general term for a recording.

clue.text: Inadmissible act after sailor's change of direction

indicators.note: after places the act and the inadmissible piece following the sailor

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
out means not allowed, as in that's out of the question
a turn is a performance or act, as in a music-hall turn

explanation.surface: A sailor changes course after behaving in a way that was not permitted.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-turn is a complete reversal, literally the military drill of turning to face the opposite way.

clue.text: New first for one who writes

parts.note: novel means new and original
1st is written first, read here as IST

explanation.surface: A novice writer has just published their debut.
explanation.walkthrough: 1ST, the short form of first, is read as the letters IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelist is an author of novels, someone who writes fiction.

clue.text: Interrupts what may be wrong in a canal boat?

definitions.meaning: to cut into someone else's conversation rudely

definitions.text: what may be wrong in a canal boat?
definitions.meaning: a wrong done aboard a flat-bottomed canal vessel could be called that vessel's sin

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as BARGE'S SIN: a misdeed committed on a canal boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who barges in intrudes abruptly, interrupting what is going on.

clue.text: Baffle loud and clumsy oaf

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loud
a lummox is a clumsy, stupid person

explanation.surface: A noisy and awkward lout leaves people bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: To flummox someone is to bewilder or confuse them completely.

clue.text: Colour of small runabout on lease?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a runabout is a small car
to let is to lease out property

explanation.surface: Asking what colour a little leased car is.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant red, one particular colour.

clue.text: State that's back in within a month

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone promises a country's leader will return inside a month.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'State that's' as the definition and gave the hidden letters no signal; 'that's' is a link and 'in' tells you to look inside 'within a month'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Middle Eastern sultanate on the Arabian Peninsula is a sovereign country, hence a state.

clue.text: Prone to tears, student ruined scary home

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate, so a student

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of these words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A student is reduced to tears because a frightening house has been wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachrymose comes from the Latin for tear and describes someone tearful or given to weeping.

clue.text: Part of airport where fugitive loses heart?

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a runaway is a fugitive who has fled

explanation.surface: An escaped convict at an airport becomes discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' drops the middle A of RUNAWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The strip on which aircraft take off and land is a key section of any airfield.

clue.text: Tense, being over border

parts.note: on can mean over, as in a lid on a jar or a talk on a subject
an edge is a border or margin

explanation.surface: Someone feels nervous after crossing a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nervous and jumpy is idiomatically described as being on edge.

clue.text: Remains confused about origin of rock salts

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumble goes round the single letter
confused means jumbled, so the letters of remains are mixed
the origin of a word is where it starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: A puzzling account of what is left around the source of some rock salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salts' looks like a chemistry term after 'rock', but old salts are sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a seasoned sailor, so salts are seamen.

clue.text: Regret accepting Liberal convention

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the liberal goes inside the regret

parts.note: to rue is to regret
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in British politics

explanation.surface: Remorse at agreeing to a Liberal party conference.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule is an established practice or norm, as in 'as a rule', so a convention.

clue.text: V can be progress, in a way

indicators.note: in places the progress inside the letters for a way

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to gain is to make progress, and a gain is an advance

explanation.surface: A single letter could stand for advancement along a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'V' stands for versus, as in a fixture list.
explanation.definitionFit: V is the abbreviation for versus, the Latin word for opposed to, as in Arsenal v Spurs.

clue.text: Generally succeeded finding something to wear

parts.note: overall means generally, taken as a whole
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone has largely managed to locate an item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is singular but the answer is plural: overalls are one garment, a pair, like trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls are a protective one-piece work garment, an item of clothing.

clue.text: On review, sign it, ideally retaining process of redaction

indicators.note: on review means looked back over, so the held letters run from right to left
retaining means holding within, so the letters lie inside these words

explanation.surface: Advice that, after reading a document again, you should ideally sign it.
explanation.definitionFit: Redaction is the preparing or revising of text for publication, which is what an editor does.
